ideas: Less free time because of work and family
Fewer natural places to meet new people
Adults becoming more cautious and selective

phrases.meaning: be the one to start contact
try hard to make something work

model: I'd say the main reason is time. At school or university, you're surrounded by people who are the same age and who share your schedule, so friendships almost happen automatically. After twenty-five, most people are juggling work and family, and they're often stuck in a routine that goes from office to home and back. There simply aren't many places where you meet strangers regularly and naturally find common ground. I'm noticing this myself at the moment. Most of my close friends are still the ones from university, and although I get on well with colleagues, it takes much longer to really open up to them. Another reason is that adults are more cautious. We're less willing to make the first move because we're afraid of seeming desperate. That said, I don't think it's impossible. People who join clubs or volunteer groups can still build a tight-knit group and a real sense of belonging. It just means you have to put in the effort deliberately rather than waiting for it to happen.
